svg.desc: Banner for a moment obstruction and minimal-degree polynomial nonconforming Stokes elements on tetrahedra. Left: a tetrahedron drawn in perspective with one face shaded; its degrees of freedom are face moments, averages over each face F of v times q for every test polynomial q of degree n, and cell moments against polynomials of degree n − 1 at an interior point. For fourth order, n = 3, there are N = 50 moments. Middle: a degree ladder for n = 3. Each rung shows 50 squares, one per moment. On P4 = P(n+1), of dimension 35, the moments are injective, so 35 of the 50 directions are reached and no nonzero polynomial is hidden. On P5 = P(n+2), of dimension 56, the moments have a 7-dimensional kernel, so their rank is 56 − 7 = 49 and exactly one of the 50 directions is missing, marked in a warm colour. On P6 = P(n+3) all 50 directions are reached. Below: the kernel on P(n+2) is 7-dimensional for every n, so the rank is C(n + 5, 3) − 7. Right: the number of directions missed by degree n + 2 for n = 1 to 6 is (n − 1)(n − 2)/2, namely 0, 0, 1, 3, 6 and 10, drawn as triangular arrays of dots, so degree n + 2 suffices only for n = 1 and 2 while degree n + 3 always succeeds. A callout shows the repair for n = 3: one sextic bubble, the Vandermonde product Delta4 = product of (lambda j − lambda i) over the barycentric coordinates, whose alternating face functional A(Delta4) = 1/34650 is nonzero, while A vanishes on all quintics. In two dimensions the corresponding count is never deficient. The counts are the exact values of the paper’s Theorem 2.1 and proposition; the tetrahedron is a schematic.
